opening.headline: To determine how much data is left for your Assistant that handles sensitive data, you should read your enterprise plan's instructions with four questions: Archive, Learn Usage, Delete, and Organization Data.
body: If you are using an assistant that handles customer information, it is difficult to operate with confidence if you do not know how much conversation history is left, whether it really disappears when you press the delete button, and whether the information you enter is used to learn the model. Moreover, these terms vary depending on the plan and product.

In this class, we'll outline the questions to ask in data retention and learn how to read enterprise guidance from OpenAI and Anthropic. We then look at the differences between consumer and commercial products, exceptions to policy violations and feedback, and explain how the customer information assistant's retention settings affect operations.

visual.alt: An illustration of four question marks surrounding an assistant who handles customer information.
labels: If I delete it, does it really disappear?
Is it used for model training?

paragraphs: One team is creating and using an assistant that organizes customer consultation content. The conversation includes the customer's name and inquiry details. However, no one knows exactly how long this conversation record remains in the service.

It's not clear whether pressing the delete button actually disappears. Even though it appears to disappear from the screen, I have never checked what happens on the server. It is also unclear whether the input you entered will be used to train the model.

What is more difficult is that this condition is not set in stone. Even if the product is from the same company, the guidance is different depending on whether it is for consumer or business use and what plan it is. This class is a time to establish a framework for reading the differences.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: What questions does the belief that ‘it must be safe because it is a corporate plan’ answer and which questions it does not answer? Check it out by following along with the class.

screens.outro: First, let me recall whether I have ever checked the data storage conditions.

screens.title: Have you ever checked how much of your conversation history is kept?
screens.lead: If you first think about each question in your head and then select it, the instructor will organize your thoughts. You will not enter or submit an answer.

items.prompt: Have you ever wondered where and how much of your business AI's conversations are stored?
items.answer: Most people are too busy using it to look for it. However, the retention period is specifically written in the product instructions. Inserting sensitive data without verification is the biggest risk.

items.prompt: Did you think that if you delete it, everything will be immediately erased?
items.answer: Many people think so. However, the timing of when it disappears from the screen and when it is cleared from the server may vary. In this class, you'll see how real-world guidance makes the distinction.

items.prompt: Did you know that if you have a corporate plan, the information you enter will not be used for learning?
items.answer: The default values are guided that way. But default also means there are exceptions. You can make an accurate decision by knowing which actions create exceptions.

screens.outro: Now, let’s start by summarizing the questions that need to be asked when it comes to data retention.

screens.title: Four questions to ask in data retention
screens.lead: As you select each question, an explanation will unfold. No matter what product you read, it's easy to compare if you use these four questions as a guideline.

items.prompt: Question 1. Archiving: How much of my conversations and files are stored?
items.answer: Storage periods vary by product and plan. Among Anthropic commercial products, the API automatically deletes input and output within 30 days after receiving it, and products that save and continue conversations keep the conversations for product experience. OpenAI's Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu inform customers that they control how much data is kept.

items.prompt: Question 2. Whether to use training: Are inputs and outputs used to train the model?
items.answer: OpenAI informs you that business data is not used for learning by default, and data accessed through apps is not used for learning by default. Anthropic also states that it does not use the input and output of commercial products for learning. In both places, exceptions are made when the user explicitly consents or sends feedback.

items.prompt: Question 3. Deletion: When deleted, is the time it disappears from the screen and the time it is deleted from the server the same?
items.answer: It may not be the same. When you delete a conversation from Anthropic commercial products, it disappears from your history immediately but is deleted from backend storage within 30 days. Operators receiving requests for deletion must be aware of and inform of this time difference.

items.prompt: Question 4: Organizational data: who owns and controls it?
items.answer: OpenAI informs enterprise products that inputs and outputs are owned by the customer and access rights are determined by the customer. Customer controls which internal materials are linked. Deciding what to do with your organization's data starts with determining who has control.

screens.outro: Let's read the actual corporate plan guide with these four questions.

screens.title: Read our Enterprise Plan Guide: OpenAI and Anthropic
screens.lead: Select each tab to see how both companies' business guidance answers the first four questions.

tabs.label: OpenAI Promise
tabs.body: OpenAI makes several promises for business data on its ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, Healthcare, Edu, Teachers and API platforms. The data is owned and controlled by the customer and is basically not used for model training. Inputs and outputs are owned by Customer to the extent permitted by law. The customer also determines which internal data will be linked and who will have access to it. Retention periods are controlled by the customer at Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu.

tabs.label: OpenAI’s GPT and apps
tabs.body: OpenAI advises that workspace members can create GPTs and share them internally with each other, and the same promises apply. If an administrator makes a GPT publicly shareable, externally published GPTs may be subject to additional review. Apps send and retrieve information from connected internal sources and external services, administrators control active apps, and each user must authenticate to the app before use. By default, data accessed through the app is not used for learning.

tabs.label: Anthropic commercial products
tabs.body: Anthropic's commercial products (Claude for Work, API, etc.) do not use input and output for learning by default. The API automatically deletes input and output from the backend within 30 days after receiving them, except in cases where there is a separate agreement, when using a service that stores them longer, or when complying with the law. Products that store conversations archive them to ensure a consistent experience, and when a user deletes them, they immediately disappear from history and are deleted from the backend within 30 days.

tabs.label: Exceptions and Feedback
tabs.body: Explicitly providing feedback or allowing data to be used can be used for learning. Any conversations you send through the Feedback button at Anthropic will be archived in their entirety for up to 5 years. Owners of Team and Enterprise plans can turn off member feedback submission by setting the Rate chats setting in Data and Privacy in Organization settings. Teams that work with sensitive material may want to consider this setting.

screens.outro: Next, we will look specifically at how guidance varies depending on the plan and exception storage.

screens.title: It varies depending on the plan and there are exceptions.
screens.lead: Below is a summary of our conservation guidance, organized for illustrative purposes. Select a highlighted passage to see its operational implications.

data.text:
Summary of Preservation Guidelines for Anthropic's Commercial Products (Concise Overview)
API input and output are automatically deleted from the backend within 30 days of receipt.
Products such as Claude for Work store conversations within the product itself.
When a user deletes a conversation, It disappears from your records immediately and is deleted from our servers within 30 days.
Conversations marked as violating policy may have their input and output stored for up to two years.
Conversations sent through the feedback button are stored for up to 5 years.
It may be stored longer if required by law.

marks.span: API input and output are automatically deleted from the backend within 30 days of receipt.
marks.note: This is the default per API user. Exceptions are made when using a longer-term storage service, when there is a separate agreement, or when policy enforcement and compliance with the law are necessary. Even within the same company, guidance for APIs and interactive products are different.

marks.span: It disappears from your records immediately and is deleted from our servers within 30 days.
marks.note: The deletion time on the screen and on the server are different. When a customer requests deletion, it would be inaccurate to reply that “everything has been deleted immediately.” We must also provide information on how long it will take to delete the server.

marks.span: Conversations marked as violating policy may have their input and output stored for up to two years.
marks.note: Normal retention periods do not apply to conversations that our automated safety systems mark as policy violations. Inputs and outputs can be stored for up to 2 years, and safety classification results can be stored for up to 7 years.

marks.span: Conversations sent through the feedback button are stored for up to 5 years.
marks.note: Feedback is an exception path to learning usage. If you press the feedback button in a consultation conversation, the conversation may be stored for a long time, so you are instructed not to press it in conversations containing customer information, or the administrator turns off the function.

marks.span: It may be stored longer if required by law.
marks.note: The retention period may be longer if necessary to address legal obligations or resolve disputes. It is important to remember that the base period in the guidance is a typical period and not a minimum standard.

screens.outro: Now that we have checked the exceptions, we will explain the settings for the customer information assistant.

screens.title: Explanation: Retention Settings for Customer Information Assistant
screens.lead: The instructor first asks the Customer Information Assistant in question four questions to organize retention settings. Select the arrows to advance one step at a time.

steps.title: 1. Divide data types
steps.body: Data entering the assistant is divided into conversations, uploaded files, and feedback. This is because the conditions for preservation and learning use may vary for each type. Feedback is an exception path to learning usage and is therefore addressed separately.

steps.title: 2. Check retention period and controllable plan
steps.body: Establish a retention period that fits your organization's policies. To do this, you must first check whether the plan you are using allows you to control retention. For OpenAI, Enterprise, Healthcare, and Edu, customers control retention periods. For other plans, determine whether you can accept the basic terms and conditions provided.

steps.title: 3. Check learning usage defaults and feedback
steps.body: Ensure that the default is to disable learning, preventing any behavior that would result in an exception. We advise you not to include customer information in the feedback button, and if you are a Claude Team or Enterprise, consider turning off member feedback submission through the rate chats settings.

steps.title: 4. Write down the deletion point in operational documents.
steps.body: We write in the operational documentation that the deletion will be reflected immediately on the screen, but will be completed on the server after a certain period of time. We also prepare language responding to customer requests for deletion in accordance with this fact.

steps.title: Instructor's judgment
steps.body: Let me answer your first question. The data of this assistant is stored according to the instructions of the plan you use, is not used for learning by default, and deletion is completed immediately from history and within the specified period from the server. Documenting this basis is the starting point of operation.

screens.outro: Now let's compare the operational impact of retention settings.

screens.title: Commentary: How retention settings impact operations
screens.lead: Select the two states alternately and compare the pros and cons of keeping the preservation period short and long.

states.label: short retention
states.body: A short retention period reduces the risk of exposure by ensuring no outdated conversations remain. However, it makes it difficult to reference previous conversations and create an audit trail to determine what happened when something goes wrong. When the same customer inquires again, it is difficult to continue the previous context. It is suitable for work where you do not want to hold on to personal information for a long time. However, keeping it short does not mean that data already sent as feedback or subject to legal storage will disappear.

states.label: long preservation
states.body: A longer retention period ensures that the history remains for context and review. Instead, when a leak occurs, the impact increases, and when a deletion request comes in, there are more things to deal with. When responding to a deletion request, you must also provide information on how long it will take for the deletion to be completed from our servers. Select only if your resume is absolutely necessary for the job. Finding a balance between policy and operational needs and documenting your reasons makes them easier to explain later.

screens.outro: Lastly, let me summarize the main points.

screens.title: Retention conditions vary depending on the plan
screens.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.

paragraphs: Data retention in enterprise plans should not be read as one set of rules, but as the answer to four questions: Retention, Learning Availability, Deletion, and Organizational Data. And the answer depends on the product and plan.

When reading default values, exceptions are also read. Data may be retained longer or used for learning to send feedback, flag policy violations, or if required by law. Setting retention is a balance between exposure risk and business needs.

callout.label: something to remember
callout.text: Check whether learning is used and when to delete it separately. Read defaults and exceptions together.

checks.q: What happens when a user deletes a conversation in Anthropic commercial products?
options: It disappears from your records immediately and is cleared from the backend within 30 days.
Everything is deleted at the same moment in the backend.
All conversations are kept for 5 years
Remains on screen until administrator approval
checks.explain: Deleted conversations are removed from your history immediately, but are removed from our servers within 30 days.

wrong.1: The point at which it disappears from the screen and the point at which the server is deleted are not the same.
wrong.2: The 5-year retention exception applies to conversations where explicit feedback is sent.
wrong.3: After deletion, it disappears from history immediately and is not dependent on administrator approval.

checks.intro: Check for yourself what you just learned. Results are not recorded.

checks.q: What is the right judgment when setting retention conditions for assistants handling customer information?
options: Consider the preservation conditions of all plans to be the same and check them only once.
It varies depending on the plan, product, and role, so check the instructions for the plan you are using separately.
Once you check whether or not to use learning, you do not need to check when to delete it.
There are no exceptions to the retention period, even conversations marked as policy violations.
checks.explain: Preservation conditions vary by plan and product, so you must check them based on the plan you are using, and the timing of learning use and deletion is also looked at separately.

wrong.0: There are separate instructions for consumer and commercial products, and control availability also varies depending on the plan.
wrong.2: Whether to use learning and when to delete it are separate questions and must be checked separately.
wrong.3: There is an exception for policy-violating conversations where input and output can be stored for up to 2 years.

glossary.def: This is the period and conditions under which conversations and files will be stored on the server.
Whether the inputs and outputs are used to improve the model.
The conditions for deletion include the scope of deletion by the user and the point at which it is completely deleted from the server.
Business input, output, and files that the organization owns and has control over.

misconceptions.myth: If you delete it, everything disappears immediately.
misconceptions.fact: Although it may disappear from your screen immediately, it will take a specified period of time for it to be removed from our servers. In Anthropic commercial products, backend deletion occurs within 30 days.

misconceptions.myth: If it's a corporate plan, it's always guaranteed that it won't be used for learning.
misconceptions.fact: The default is to not use it for training, but exceptions are made if the user explicitly allows it, such as by sending feedback or agreeing to use their data.

misconceptions.myth: The retention conditions for all plans are the same.
misconceptions.fact: There are separate guidelines for consumer and commercial products, and the ability to control retention also varies depending on the plan. You must check the instructions for the plan you are using directly.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: Retention conditions vary by product and plan.
Check whether learning is used and when to delete it separately.
There are exceptions for retention of feedback and policy violations.
Retention settings are a balance between exposure risk and business needs.
